short: A disastrous Athenian military campaign during the Peloponnesian War that crippled their naval power.
full:
In 415 BCE, during a fragile peace in the Peloponnesian War, Athens launched a massive armada to conquer Syracuse on the island of Sicily. Championed by Alcibiades but ultimately commanded by the cautious Nicias, the expedition was plagued by logistical failures and indecisive leadership. Syracuse, aided by the Spartan general Gylippus, successfully defended the city and turned the tables, besieging the Athenian besiegers in their own camps.

The campaign ended in total catastrophe for Athens in 413 BCE. The entire expeditionary force, comprising thousands of hoplites and hundreds of ships, was destroyed or captured, and its commanders executed. The disaster shattered the myth of Athenian naval supremacy, severely depleted their treasury, and emboldened their enemies across the Aegean.
